source_row.rationale: A distinctive "slapped cheek" facial rash followed by a lacy, reticular (net-like) rash on the trunk and extremities is the classic presentation of erythema infectiosum (fifth disease), caused by parvovirus B19. This is generally a mild, self-limited illness in healthy children, though it can pose risks to pregnant individuals (fetal risk) and those with certain blood disorders or immunocompromise.
